summary: R-37: the base is the local mainline when it is ahead of the remote one. `aegis land` moves the local ref and the push comes after; between the two the landed work sits between `origin/main` and `main` with its task marked merged, and `default_base` diffed against the remote — so the framework's own pre-push gate refused the push of the first landing it ever met (TASK-FIRSTHOUR-01, eight files "belong to no task"), and the next task claimed before the push would have inherited the landed files as its diff. One rule in `core.default_base` with a helper that maps `origin/<name>` (and `origin/HEAD` through its symref) to the local name; two ARCHITECTURE passages say it. No new state.

verification.command: R-27 reverse run: test_the_push_of_a_landing_passes_the_pre_push_gate against a git archive of 137f64a
verification.note: red there with "belongs to no task"

invalidated_assumptions: "a merged task owns nothing because its work is behind default_base" — true only once the landing is pushed; between land and push the remote is behind and the rule orphaned the landed files
